# SO-101 follower arm model (vendored)

- **Source:** https://github.com/TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100, directory `Simulation/SO101/`
- **Commit:** `a758567c3978dfeefe282ede0500085a48fe8f78` (main, 2026-10-06)
- **License:** Apache-2.0 (copy in `LICENSE`, fetched from the same commit)
- **Files taken verbatim:** `so101_new_calib.urdf` and the 13 meshes it references, in `assets/`
  (`base_motor_holder_so101_v1`, `base_so101_v2`, `sts3215_03a_v1`, `sts3215_03a_no_horn_v1`,
  `waveshare_mounting_plate_so101_v2`, `motor_holder_so101_base_v1`, `rotation_pitch_so101_v1`,
  `upper_arm_so101_v1`, `under_arm_so101_v1`, `motor_holder_so101_wrist_v1`,
  `wrist_roll_pitch_so101_v2`, `wrist_roll_follower_so101_v1`, `moving_jaw_so101_v1`; `.stl`).
- "new_calib" = LeRobot's current calibration convention (each joint's zero at the middle of its
  range), so sim joint angles line up with `so101_follower` readings in degrees -> radians
  (gripper excepted: LeRobot reports it as 0-100, the URDF as an angle; mapping is WO-06).

## Edits (all generated by `build_collision.py`, output `so101.urdf` — the file the agent loads)

1. **Jaw collision geometry.** PhysX uses the convex hull of each collision mesh. The hull of
   `wrist_roll_follower_so101_v1.stl` (fixed jaw + wrist-roll body) fills the gap between the
   jaws, so nothing can be grasped. Both jaw meshes are cut into slabs along the finger
   (5 finger slabs + 1 body piece each) and each slab is replaced by its convex hull
   (<= 64 vertices) in `collision/fixed_jaw_*.stl` / `collision/moving_jaw_*.stl`. Visual meshes
   and all other collision meshes are unchanged.
2. **`tcp_link`** (massless, fixed to `gripper_link` at `xyz = (0.0068, 0, -0.092)`): the centre
   of a 3 cm cube clamped against the fixed-jaw tip, 13 mm above the fingertips. Axes: z =
   approach (out of the fingers), y = closing direction (fixed jaw -> moving jaw).
3. Robot name `so101_new_calib` -> `so101`; a provenance comment at the top.

Joint names, limits, origins, inertias and visual meshes are exactly upstream.
